and the rapporteur on reform, mr van hulten. today we are debating the discharge for 1998. to this end, the european treaty requires parliament to examine the accounts and financial statements, the annual report of the court of auditors and the replies provided by the bodies subject to audit. in its report on the 1998 financial year, presented in november last year, the court of auditors gave the commission a statement of assurance as regards revenue and commitment appropriations. the court of auditors has not given its assurance as to the legality and regularity of the execution of the payments. the percentage of errors or omissions found was considered by the court to be too high. as the commissioner responsible for the budget, i fully share the view that in some areas budgetary execution gaps are simply unacceptable. that is why i immediately took the initiative, with my services, to draw up an action plan which provides, sector by sector, for concrete measures based on a concrete timetable in order to reduce the number of errors detected. almost 90% of all errors found or deduced by the court of auditors relate to the member states. most payments from the eu budget are not made directly by the brussels administration but by the administrative units of the member states. this decentralisation of budget implementation has many advantages, but on the other hand it naturally requires excellent and close cooperation. as rapporteur for the sem 2000 and decentralised management measures, mr kuhne has dealt with these issues very closely and i thank him for his work in this area. in its discharge debate in 1998, the council - which recommended discharge to the commission - took up the issues of shared management and proposed that member states should perhaps set themselves a target of reducing the gaps in the implementation of community funds - a very interesting proposal. the commission will also redouble its efforts to make the financial regulations more flexible for the member states' administrations and to provide advice and information, in particular on control systems, or to use, if necessary, the monetary leverage of financial correction mechanisms for refunds to member states, as is the case in agriculture. the fact that the percentage of errors in agricultural expenditure is much lower than that found in the framework of the structural funds may be due to this financial instrument. my colleague franz fischler will come back to this in more detail in a moment, but i take this opportunity to thank mr casaca for his report and to express my deep respect for mr mulder's report. the court of auditors has not made any criticisms of the budget of the european coal and steel community and i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr khanbhai, for the report he has just presented. the court also gave its statement of assurance on the implementation of the budget of the european development fund, accompanied, however, by some critical observations. overall, there was a marked decrease in the percentage of errors for this fund compared with previous years. however, this is by no means an excuse for the commission to indulge in complacency. the commission, on the contrary, intends to achieve more satisfactory results with regard to this financial instrument which is really very important for development policy, and this concerns in particular the question of the speed of aid. you mentioned it, mr van den berg. i was not aware of it. this is also in line with the rapporteur's concern in this area and i would like to thank you very warmly, mrs rühle, for your willingness to take up the arguments of the committee on development and cooperation and the commission in your report and to propose an action plan. i would also like to take this opportunity to thank mr blak for his preparatory work in this area. the legislative, budgetary and control powers of the various institutions overlap more within the european union than in the member states. cooperation is therefore essential to the functioning of the european union and presupposes a clear and reliable distribution of roles. that is why the discussions and negotiations currently taking place between parliament and the commission on the agreement which also deals with the issue of access to and treatment of confidential information are of paramount importance. the president of the committee on budgetary control, mrs theato, has a special role to play in this respect. it is in the interest of all of us that these negotiations should lead - and i hope this will be soon - to a result which will allow for good policy and good cooperation on issues of the importance of the discharge. the commission is committed to transparency and openness. for the commission, this is not an empty phrase. that is why i have forwarded to the committee on budgetary control or to the rapporteur, in the context of the discharge procedure, all the confidential control reports which have been requested from me. therefore, the commission also replied to the questionnaires in detail, even if this was not the usual practice. the commission has nothing to hide and it feels it has a duty to give parliament its full support in the discharge of its duties. we need a procedure that guarantees the confidentiality of information and, above all, the rule of law, which excludes any prior conviction of the persons concerned. this must apply to the staff of the commission as well as to the members of the other european institutions and to all citizens. in the report adopted by the committee on budgetary control, the commission is asked to answer various questions or to take immediate action before 15 may. i would like to thank the committee on budgetary control for this resolution and for the time constraint attached to it. some of these points concern the handling of so-called old cases, i.e. cases of irregularities or suspected corruption from previous years. i would like to make it very clear from this platform that the commission is doing everything in its power to fight corruption and this is not just about the future but also about solving past cases. this commission is not afraid of any revelation. in the cresson/berthelot case, it proved this by sending documents to the courts, initiating disciplinary proceedings, lifting the immunity of a former member of the commission, of course giving the investigating judge access to the commission's premises and demanding the reimbursement of community resources granted. but, as i said, the commission is committed to the rule of law, which means that it cannot of course influence judicial proceedings, even if it is unsatisfactory to note that, in the echo case, for example, the competent courts have not yet taken any action, although the cases have been submitted to them for a long time. however, this also means that the requirement of proportionality is necessary in the case of penalties and refund claims, including commission requirements and refund claims made by member states. the european court of justice has once again clearly confirmed this in its judgment a few weeks ago on the reduction or even suspension of fines in the cement cartel case. my colleague, mr franz fischler, will come back to the agricultural budget issues connected with landfilling in a moment. but i would like to say that i do not consider that a letter to the commission indicating that a measure envisaged by the commission threatens a company with bankruptcy or could lead to job losses constitutes an illegal attempt to intervene, whether that letter comes from parliament or a member state, whether it comes from france, ireland or bavaria. it is clear that these decisions must be taken where there is a margin of appreciation, in accordance with clear regulations and in a transparent manner. i shall make sure that the financial regulation is clear. the commission will of course take note of what the court of auditors recommends or discovers in the fléchard case and i can only say that i am very grateful to the court of auditors for having undertaken this task. at this stage i cannot go into detail on the various points of the resolution. however, the commission will inform olaf as soon as it requests it, and i have already started the administrative investigation to clarify this. in the resolution you insist above all on reducing the percentage of errors in the implementation of the budget. i can assure you that the commission is continually working towards that goal. that is why we have presented the action plan, which sets out concrete measures with a concrete timetable. that is why we are carrying out a complete revision of the financial regulation and i will inform parliament about this in the near future. the european anti-fraud office is therefore being strengthened. this is why the commission has tackled the reform of financial management as a whole by making all those who manage european taxpayers' money more accountable, improving efficiency and with the clear aim of regaining confidence in the european institutions. the commission will take all the necessary steps to ensure the success of the reform and it would be good if all the european institutions were open to such reforms.

in writing. - (de) if the creation of a european refugee fund were to aim at humanizing and opening up the policy of the member states of the union in the field of asylum and the reception of refugees, that would be a welcome step. the fund, which simply merges three budget lines, will not take such a step. the debate is not the only one that has shown what the creation of the european refugee fund was really about, namely 'burden sharing'. interpreting immigration of people seeking eu protection as a 'burden' that needs to be 'shared' is a fundamentally wrong approach. on this basis, it is impossible to develop a policy which takes account of the human rights interests of persecuted and displaced persons. as the recent incorporation of a 're-admission clause' into the lomé convention has shown, the policy of the member states and the union is based on the containment and return of refugees. if this is what the outline of european asylum and immigration policy looks like and if refugees are perceived as a 'burden', the creation of a refugee fund is a cosmetic measure designed to hide the real face: that of a european policy of containment. in this form, the fund does not encourage any state to shift its policy towards greater openness towards the entry of refugees. nor can it improve the legal security of persecuted people who seek our protection. yet this is precisely what should be at stake, along with the rights of refugees to associate and participate. the european union calls for the free movement of capital worldwide. but it does reduce people's freedom a little bit more by closing borders and blocking refugees and asylum seekers. every year, many refugees die, are murdered, at the eu's external borders. in this context, it is illusory to imagine that the creation of a refugee fund would humanize asylum and refugee reception policy. that's why i abstained.

counsel. - (pt) madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the work of the intergovernmental conference is proceeding at a very rapid pace, this time with the increased participation of the european parliament through the president and two other representatives, through a very intensive dialogue between the presidency and the committee on constitutional affairs of this parliament and also thanks to direct information and the debate in plenary of the european parliament, which is unprecedented and very promising as regards the future results of the conference. five major in-depth meetings of the preparatory group and three meetings of the intergovernmental conference itself have been held to date. all events on the calendar will take place by the end of the semester, both for the conference and the preparatory group. the report which will be presented to the feira european council will not be a mere academic report, but a positive report, a report which will enable the next presidency, the french presidency, to continue to develop this work with a view to reaching a decision at the end of the year. the point we discussed at the last intergovernmental conference was the question of extending qualified majority voting. the member states have shown a certain openness, although many have not yet made a final decision. it is still possible to identify, as a preliminary point, certain provisions which arouse the negative attitude of a large majority of member states, which do not want to abandon the rule of unanimity. the debate on these subjects shows that there are still many reservations which could be overcome during the conference. the preparatory work carried out so far has also covered matters relating to the european parliament, the courts, the committee of the regions and the economic and social committee. as regards the decision-making process of the european parliament, there is a broad consensus not to proceed with a revision of the treaty which would alter the existing institutional balance. as regards the framework for the application of codecision, there is some openness to extend codecision to all cases of adoption of legislative acts by qualified majority, without however establishing any systematic correlation. as regards the court of justice and the court of first instance, a group of friends of the presidency has been set up and given the task of studying possible amendments to the treaty concerning the two courts. the examination of possible amendments to the treaty has begun in respect of the court of auditors, the economic and social committee and the committee of the regions. many believe that changes should only be made to the extent strictly necessary to ensure the effective functioning of the union after enlargement. the question of the subjects which might be included on the agenda of the conference was also discussed, on a proposal from the presidency. it should be recalled that the conclusions of the helsinki council provide that the presidency will present a report to the european council and may propose new items for the work of the conference. as regards security and defence and the charter of fundamental rights, the presidency reserves the right, depending on the progress of the work, to propose to the feira european council in june that any adjustments or additions to the treaties which may prove necessary be included in the conference. as regards other subjects which might be added to the work of the conference, a first debate was held on the basis of a list drawn up by the presidency. the argument put forward to justify a cautious approach to the inclusion of new subjects on the agenda was that the inherent technical complexity of the debate would cause a delay in the deadline for the completion of the work of the conference, december 2000. as regards the question of the size and composition of the commission, there is a consensus that the commission which emerges from this conference must be strong, independent and legitimate, and that its collegial nature must be preserved. however, there is a clear dissonance between small and medium-sized states, on the one hand, which favour a commission composed of one national from each member state, enjoying the same status, and large member states, on the other hand, which prefer a fixed number of commissioners irrespective of the number of member states. the size of the college of commissioners is the main point of contention between the delegations and determines the rest of the debate on the commission, since some of them link this point to positions concerning the composition, internal organisation and structure of the institution. as regards the individual responsibility of commissioners, the general trend is to maintain the commitment currently entered into by each commissioner to resign if the president of the commission so requests. the delegations are divided between those who wish to maintain the informal nature of this commitment and those who would like to formalize it in the treaty. as regards the collective responsibility of the commission as a college, there is a certain reluctance to amend the current institutional framework, the current control of the european parliament being considered sufficient. the idea put forward by the european parliament that the commission could ask for a vote of confidence in the institution was welcomed. on the question of the weighting of votes in the council, there is consensus on the criterion to be used as the basis for qualified majority voting in the council. it must be the result of a combination of two elements which are the foundations of the union: its population and the existence of sovereign states. our union is a union of peoples and states at the same time. as regards the concrete mechanisms to be envisaged for the future system, there is still a split between those who favour a double majority and those who simply prefer a new weighting. one of the recurring arguments is that the reform must be acceptable to public opinion and ratifiable by national parliaments, a concern shared by all member states, large and small, not only because ratification of the new treaty allows for enlargement and respect for these deadlines, but also because there is a feeling that a european crisis should not be opened up about this type of reform. it is also believed that these reforms should be presented to the public in the central and eastern european countries, the candidate countries, so as not to give the impression that these are hasty reforms, not to improve the european union, but to prevent these new member states from having access to the decision-making system of the european union. for enhanced cooperation, the question of the need or the desirability of the conference to address this topic was raised in an informal debate. there are mixed views both on the possibility of dealing with this subject and on the framework and nature of possible amendments. the next informal meeting of the representatives group, to be held on 14 and 15 june in sintra, portugal, will deal specifically with this subject. this is a difficult subject to deal with, given the lack of examples: there are no concrete examples, since the treaty of amsterdam already allows for enhanced cooperation and no member state has so far used this instrument; there are also no advanced theoretical examples in the literature; so this question is a recurring one, but it's very abstract. as regards the substance of the debate and the introduction of enhanced cooperation in the second pillar, the informal debate showed that the majority believe that there is no need to introduce it in the common foreign and security policy, while admitting that it could be used in the context of security and defence. in other words, if we are to include the theme of enhanced cooperation in the second pillar, then it will be necessary to find specific ways of implementing this concept in this area, which will not be able to copy the first pillar given the difference in functioning between the two pillars. as regards the relaxation of the existing model, advocated in particular by the commission, there is some openness towards eliminating the use of the european council in enhanced cooperation, the limit of eight member states being, however, contested by those who advocate a change in the requirement for the participation of the majority of member states. as you can see, ladies and gentlemen, the portuguese presidency is making every effort to move the work forward so that a comprehensive and balanced agreement, acceptable to all, can be reached within the timeframe. the commission and the european parliament have maintained close cooperation. as regards the latter, cooperation has been maintained both through the participation of the president and two elected members and through regular information to the committee on constitutional affairs and the plenary, which ensures that this institutional reform work is carried out with a much greater involvement of the european parliament than in the previous revision of the treaty. this bodes well for the outcome of our work.

1999, total eu aid to the countries of south-east europe, the european community and the member states combined, exceeded eur 19.3 billion. the european union is also the main trading partner of all the countries in the region. it has made substantial trade concessions to them and several thousand eu military, police and civilian workers are active in the region, particularly in kosovo. as i said, mr president, we have read with great interest the conclusions of the rapporteur on the stabilization and association process in the countries of south-east europe. the assessment of the strength and possible weaknesses of the stabilisation and association process will undoubtedly provide some food for thought, and i will try to comment on some of the elements of the report. as i said, the lisbon european council confirmed that our overall objective remains the integration of the countries of the region as far as possible into the political and economic system of europe. stabilisation and association agreements are an essential part of this policy. as the rapporteur rightly points out, these new agreements will not enter into force immediately, since we will first have to prepare, negotiate and conclude each one of them. the rapporteur concludes that it will be necessary to create a kind of medium-term regional stabilisation and development programme. i am not necessarily convinced that this analysis is the best way of dealing with the problem. the general process of stabilizing the region cannot be reduced to agreements alone. it is clear that these are the most visible and well-known part of this process, but it contains other important instruments such as, for example, preferential trade agreements, direct aid from the european union and political dialogue. these countries already enjoy trade preferences for the most part and the extraordinary lisbon council confirmed that the stability and association agreements should be seen as a form of greater asymmetric trade liberalisation favouring precisely these countries in their bilateral trade with the countries of the union. the idea behind the association and stabilisation processes is sufficiently flexible and broad to guarantee a consistent project in this field. as regards the agreements, we believe that the fact that some time is needed for their elaboration should not jeopardize the whole stabilization process. this has not been the european union's past experience in equivalent regional processes. in this way, as in other global agreements, we hope to have intermediate agreements covering the period between the signing and ratification of these agreements, given that there are normally 20 months between one agreement and another. it is also worth recalling that we have already had contractual relations in the form of trade and cooperation agreements with albania and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia. the new agreements, which are broader but also more demanding for our partners, since they include elements of political conditionality which are of course part of what is currently the matrix of the union in this field, will precisely replace the existing agreements in both cases; they will have to focus much more on regional cooperation than existing agreements and will include provisions on justice and home affairs, an area of the utmost importance for the europe of tomorrow. negotiations have already begun with the former yugoslav republic of macedonia on the stabilisation and association agreement. the albanian government has recently made known its reaction to the feasibility study on the opening of negotiations prepared by the european commission; the council will shortly be examining this report. following internal political changes, the european commission is also preparing a feasibility study for croatia, which the council hopes to be able to analyse immediately before or immediately after the summer. a road map, so to speak, has been sent to bosnia-herzegovina at the request of the local authorities. the implementation of this roadmap will contribute to the preparation of a feasibility study on the negotiation of a similar agreement. the work is proceeding well, bearing in mind, of course, that in this particular case we must be careful not to create excessive expectations, and that the local reality does not encourage us to be overly optimistic. mr president, let me briefly mention the new rules of procedure. as agreed with the european parliament, in order to create a uniform legal basis for aid to the region, the council is studying a proposal from the european commission and a regulation which will replace the aid to the region provided by the phare and obnova programmes. the recommendations will be a valuable contribution to the discussions we will be having in the council on this subject. i noted in particular that the report insists that the reconstruction of the region should not be understood as a mere physical and economic reconstruction, but should also be oriented towards social infrastructure, civil society and public institutions, which are the main objectives of our real strategy for the reconstruction of the region. it is not just a matter of material things, but of overall stabilization. the rapporteur also makes a brief reference to the stability pact which has served as the framework for cooperation with the five countries and with the countries linked to the enlargement process. the recent joint regional conference of the european commission and the world bank, organised in close cooperation with the special representative for the stability pact on financing, has given a significant boost to the pact's objective of reinvigorating reform processes and stimulating regional cooperation, and has demonstrated that the mechanism of the stability pact is mature and can and should progress. we believe that mutual commitment is the key to the success of the pact and i think that this point was made clear in the discussion we had recently at the conference organized by the european commission and the world bank. the commitment of the countries of the region to carry out institutional reforms and to create an environment conducive to economic progress is a fundamental element of this pact. in return, the international community is supporting the reform commitments, with donors and financial institutions pledging or mobilising a total of €2.4 billion. of this amount, the european union - the commission and the member states - has alone pledged or mobilised 1.08 billion. the international community funded an initial €1.8 billion package presented at the conference and provided the necessary funding to accelerate the preparation and implementation of projects and initiatives in the short-term package. but as i said, the conference was just a starting point, the first step in a long process. the european union has committed itself to playing a leading role in this area, ensuring a coherent approach to the whole process of accompaniment, and to closely accompanying and supporting regional reform processes in a way that corresponds to the efforts actually made by each country so that they are justly rewarded by progress in the process of the new instruments, in order to allow economic and social development, as well as progress in line with european schemes. with the exception of belgrade, all the governments in the region have seen fit to embark on the path of reform. i would like to make it clear, however, that the council believes that our joint efforts will be incomplete without serbia. a democratic and cooperative serbia, at peace with its neighbours, will be welcome in the european family. it must be remembered that the overall stability of the region will not be complete as long as one country in the region is a factor of instability. i would like to see this message received by serbian civil society and confirm the support given to montenegro and the efforts of its government to stabilise the country. finally, we would point out that the honourable member wishes the mandate of the european agency for reconstruction to be extended beyond kosovo. on 20 march the council invited the commission to study and submit to it a proposal to include montenegro in its mandate. at the same time, discussions are continuing on the possible expansion of the eib's activities. i would like to conclude by saying that the council has invited the secretary-general and the high representative, under the authority of the presidency of the council and in full association with the commission, to ensure the coherence of policies for the western balkans. these ideas were put forward for the first time at the last general affairs council and they are the exact result of this presentation by commissioner christopher patten and xavier solana. we are confident that this matter will be followed with the greatest attention at the forthcoming meetings of the general affairs council and that it will be accompanied by effective implementation measures.

the rapporteur. - (de) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the question of supplementary pensions in the single market is increasingly being discussed by political bodies at national and community level. it is enough to look at the preparatory work for this debate on the commission's communication to see how urgent the matter is. the problem of supplementary retirement is complex. it has implications for social policy, business, taxation and capital markets. since the publication of the green paper, the commission has focused on the question of the capital market, seeking harmonisation in the short term of the prudential rules to be enforced by pension providers. the phrase 'complementary retirement in the single market' which it uses in this connection already superficially defines the concept of retirement and opens the way to other legislative initiatives in the tax or social field and also creates a community law which exerts an influence on national case-law. it is precisely this short-term vision, this search for quick success without a long-term objective, that i criticise the commission for. the challenge is to bring real community added value to european citizens, businesses, workers, pensioners and beneficiaries by allowing them to join cross-border pension providers that guarantee a genuine retirement in the single market. it is this added value that we are seeking when we call on the commission to draw a distinction in its next legislative proposals between the mere constitution of capital and a pension scheme, in other words to draw a distinction between providers who cover biometric risks and those who merely invest capital. we share the view of legislators in many member states that a pension scheme can only be said to exist when biometric risks (disability, longevity and death) are covered. what does that mean exactly ? in the case of longevity, this means that pension providers are obliged to pay a guaranteed old age pension until the end of the insured person's life. in other words, it is not a question of giving alms to the beneficiary or reducing the amount of his pension when the risks linked to age increase. the survivors' insurance covers family members who are entitled to and dependent on the deceased's income. in the case of invalidity, the benefit is granted even if you are totally or partially unable to work. if our objective is really to support statutory old age insurance through the supplementary scheme in the single market, we cannot fail to cover these biometric risks. if this is not the case, it is a retirement pension but not a pension scheme. but it is not just the quality of pensions in europe that is at stake. when we ask for a separate legal framework for the various pension products and providers, we also have in mind, above all, legal certainty within the territory of the union and the member states and a better chance of future integration of the single market. the equalization of the different products on offer (pension benefits and old age provision) runs exactly counter to the objective of introducing a supplementary pension scheme in the single market. it is clear from this that the commission's main objective is the creation of a european capital market. some arguments about that. the introduction of deferred taxation in all member states not only makes the supplementary pension scheme more active, but is the fundamental prerequisite for cross-border economic affiliation. this means that companies - whether large or small - no longer have to pay into 15 different schemes for their employees, but into one. but tax deferral creates deficits for the member states. the only way to reach a tax consensus between member states is to define a clear legal framework at eu level - whatever the directive used for this purpose - and limit the losses incurred. for this reason, we are calling for the development of two sets of directives: one on pension schemes with compulsory cover for biometric risks and one on old age provision. the combination of the two can make the union fully integrated. as far as pensions are concerned, we have a good chance of finding a solution soon. this is why we must not be persuaded by banks and investment firms to take short-term or unambitious decisions. i would ask you, ladies and gentlemen, as co-decision-makers of the next directives, to give the commission the right signal by voting tomorrow in favour of the stability of old age insurance in the european union, in favour of a supplementary pension scheme in the single market that is worthy of the name! provisional nature of mr birdal's release, and unfortunately, rightly so. we shall therefore continue to follow this case as part of our detailed annual review. as you know, we are currently preparing an accession partnership with turkey as part of the pre-accession strategy. the document, which sets out the priorities for turkey in preparing for accession, is due to be adopted by the commission in occasions in the context of its specific bilateral dialogue with china on human rights. the situation in tibet was also one of the main topics on the agenda of the last eu-china summit, held in beijing last december. we will continue to pursue the tibet issue with the chinese authorities. as regards the death penalty in the united states, the commission is concerned, as many of you are, about the increasing number of people sentenced to death and executed in the united states since the reintroduction of the death penalty in 1976. since 1998, opposition to the death penalty has become one of the most visible elements of the eu's human rights policy as a whole. as far as the united states is concerned, we are in constant dialogue not only with the government but also with the other relevant american authorities, and in particular with the governors of the states where the death penalty has not been abolished. the commission also welcomes the decision taken by the governor of illinois to impose a moratorium on all pending executions in that state, and we hope that this decision will mark an important step towards the abolition of the death penalty in that state. as the governor of illinois, mr ryan, has indicated, the risk of condemning innocent people to death is one of the key principles underlying the union's position on the abolition of the death penalty. and we intend, as we have begun to do, to encourage all the states in the united states which have the death penalty to reflect on this risk and to take a moratorium measure similar to that which has been taken in illinois with a view to achieving abolition of the death penalty throughout the country. as regards the more specific case of juan miguel garza, the commission is currently working to clarify the facts through our delegation in washington. on the basis of these clarifications, the commission will decide whether, in the light of the 1998 guidelines, a specific approach to the us authorities is required. the us authorities must expect this; they are fully aware of the opposition of the union as a whole to the death penalty and to any execution. the last item is the one on zimbabwe. i shall briefly return to the four points which were raised during the debate: the elections, the fate of our cooperation, the intervention in the democratic republic of the congo and, finally, the violence perpetrated in connection with the land reform. as regards the elections, our main concern is the organization of free and democratic elections. as regards the possibility of sending a team of eu election observers, the commission acknowledges the long experience of the european parliament and the acp-eu joint assembly in this kind of exercise and in particular of a number of members of parliament who are present here and who have spoken in this debate. however, we doubt the effectiveness of such an initiative given the uncertainties surrounding the preparation of the elections. at this stage, one way to help would be to step up our activities at the local level in terms of civic education, local training and election observation; the commission has entered the final phase of a project to train more than a thousand local election monitors and we have been in contact with our partners in the southern african development community, sadec, to define their role and to see if sending a sadec observation team could be considered. as regards the question that has been raised about the possible suspension of our cooperation, we consider that although there may be grounds for suspending financial cooperation with zimbabwe under the lomé convention, we are of the opinion, for the time being, as mrs maes is of the opinion, that such a measure would be contrary to the aim pursued before the elections. the poor macroeconomic performance of the government, the commission, the imf and the world bank have already led to the suspension of support for structural adjustment, and the donors involved in land reform have also suspended their institutional cooperation projects. we have done so, as far as we are concerned, but we continue to support programmes to resettle people to combat poverty and we believe that the aid for the fight against poverty which has been approved under the 8th edf in the social sectors should be maintained. as regards zimbabwe's intervention in the democratic republic of congo, we support the lusaka peace agreement which calls for a status quo of forces present and a cessation of hostilities in accordance with the terms of that agreement. finally, as regards land reform, since february the union has responded in various ways to the recent deplorable events in the country, allegedly at the instigation of the zimbabwean commission. - mr president, the commission has been actively involved in the preparation of the forum both through the evaluation of education for all 2000 and in the regional preparatory meetings, in particular in johannesburg in 1999, and the commission will be represented at the dakar forum by the director-general for development. in accordance with these international commitments, community investment in education has primarily concerned basic and primary education, particularly in the context of cooperation with the acp states. thus, a large proportion of the education programmes financed under the 8th edf were allocated to primary education. the funds allocated under this heading represent 80% of the total amount allocated to education. the commission has incorporated the recommendations of the jomtien conference on basic education into all its policy and strategy documents on education and, in the context of the national indicative programmes, 35 out of 71 acp countries have chosen education as a priority. i should point out, however, that while a balanced approach requires that priority be given to basic education, as has been said, it must not neglect the other levels of the education system. as regards the effectiveness of our approach to education, we agree that it requires very close coordination between the community and the member states and with other donors. however, we believe that dialogue with civil society is also necessary and it is in this context that the community will support the national action plans in the acp countries in the field of education. we also pursue the objective of eliminating disparities between people by 2005, in line with the strategy of the oecd development assistance committee and the conclusions of the european union social summits. the last point on the question by mr van den berg is the doubling of the budget for basic education in 2001. we believe that the community and the member states should allocate more resources to education overall and in particular to basic education. however, we also know that this can only have the desired effect if the receiving country has the necessary absorption capacity and resources to ensure the sustainability and durability of this system. so the answer is not no, it's not totally yes either. we believe that an adequate analysis of the problem requires a country-by-country examination so that this is tailored to the individual case.

(de) mr president, commissioner, as observers of the european parliament, my colleague georg jarzembowski and i were able to follow the taiwanese presidential elections on 18 march, live, if i may say so. the many conversations we had with different parties and visits to polling stations convinced us that the elections were free and democratic. we felt that the elections in taiwan were an expression of a growing democratic consciousness among the people. this is indicated by the high turnout, which increased by 6% compared to the presidential election to 82%, as well as the result as such. after a very long period of domination by the ruling party for over fifty years, the political scene has become alive. the opposition candidate was elected president and, for the first time in taiwan's history, a woman was elected vice president. these events alone are evidence of a historic turning point. the people of taiwan have taken note of the attempts of outside influence with the sensitivity of a seismograph. if the result is, of course, essentially an expression of a domestic political debate - - (de) mr president, madam commissioner, by giving discharge to the commission or refusing to give discharge, parliament examines the regularity of administrative expenditure. we all know now that there have been irregularities in the past within the commission. in addition, each report of the court of auditors emphasizes the decisive role of the member states in the allocation of the community's financial resources. this distribution leads to a very suggestive percentage of errors attributable to the member states, especially since a considerable percentage of this total is attributable to cases of fraud. the result has been the creation of an anti-fraud instrument, which we call olaf and which is not only internal to the commission. olaf is the result of the working methods of the member states and the commission and should assume an objective role in order to avoid the sources of these errors. european measures such as the introduction of the euro require the eu to prove its european competence vis-à-vis the outside because the counterfeiting of money that accompanies this introduction, for example, is an external affair. however, as regards the error rates, the deeper causes clearly lie in the different enforcement systems in force in the member states. first, the legal texts often show differences in their conception and allow for quite different legal definitions of the concept of fraud. it opens the door to fraud. just think of the example of vat collection. olaf cannot in any case be reduced to a kind of help desk. olaf cannot be a diy show on the subject of 'how to set up my own small train network'? this is a subject that cannot be treated lightly. the protection of the union's interests and, therefore, the fight against fraud are an absolute necessity. they require a homogeneous instrument which operates independently, preventively, deterrently and effectively. this requires transparent regulations, both internally and externally, so that everyone knows why they exist. i like to give this financial instrument an additional name, that of prosecutor, including a european financial prosecutor with a large body. this prosecutor must play an active role which is accepted by the member states and at the same time must be integrated into the national judicial system of the member states. i would also remind you that we have already asked for an external committee on budgetary discipline in a resolution adopted on 19 january. i think this is a good idea, not only worthy of consideration but also necessary for the creation of a comprehensive judicial and legal framework. a neutral and objective judgment serves the case and the persons concerned, which is not the case with a conviction pronounced by colleagues. olaf is therefore not a big brother loosely inspired by orson welles: its missions are confined within the limits of the rule of law. the rights of parliamentarians in matters of immunity, for example, are of course still protected. i therefore call on the intergovernmental conference to accept our request. we are discussing technical measures which we hope will not become an unquenchable fire. we must refocus on european values so that our money is not diverted, for example, to war. i know it's difficult to pass on an ideal and a virtue to another man. but this is where we should be concentrating our efforts. because lack of value leads to impotence.

commission - (de) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the fight against fraud and the protection of the communities' financial interests are among the main priorities of the new commission. the fight against fraud covers activities such as the prevention, updating and prosecution of customs and subsidy fraud or tax evasion but also, of course, updating and prosecution of irregularities within the bodies of the european union. however, i am very pleased that many of the contributions to this debate have stressed the need to distinguish between financial irregularities and fraud. when we talk about the court of auditors' report, we cover the whole spectrum of financial irregularities. we are talking about the uclaf report, or rather olaf's report, on fraud, that is to say, on intentional damage to the financial interests of the european union. the report before you, which is the subject of the bösch report, is the last report produced by uclaf in 1998 on the fight against fraud. although uclaf had only 120 staff at the time, this annual report nevertheless shows, in my view, the substantial progress made in this work. during 1998, uclaf, in cooperation with the member states, investigated 5 318 cases of suspected irregularity or fraud and, after examination, some 20% of these cases had to be classified as fraudulent. as regards the question of why there is a difference in the findings of the court of auditors' report, i would point out that in the field of agricultural policy it was found that the irregularities stemmed - and this point was emphasized - from the differences between the member states in the obligation to notify cases of fraud and doubtful cases to the commission, which explains one of the differences between the two reports. in his speech mr blak said that the public was fed up with fraud. i regret to say that cigarettes which are not cleared or which are not taxable are still being snatched and that tax evasion is often regarded as a popular sport. we are therefore faced with a situation where we must see very clearly that we cannot reduce fraud to zero at the expense of financial interests. of course, we must do everything in our power to combat customs offences and subsidy and tax offences against the financial interests of the community. i would like to briefly touch on some of the proposals in the bösch report which are in a wider context, for example with regard to the disciplinary procedure or the chamber of the european court of auditors. in its explanations of the parliament's requests in the 1998 discharge procedure, the commission stated that it did not consider it appropriate to involve a chamber of the court of auditors or the court of justice in the provisions on disciplinary measures against staff suspected of irregularities at the expense of the budget, as the european treaties assigned specific tasks to each of these bodies. it is to the court of justice that employees may appeal against a decision taken in disciplinary proceedings. such a proposal could not therefore be adapted to the present treaties. the commission has therefore chosen to take up the proposals contained in the report of the independent experts, which was submitted last year and is very extensive and covers all aspects of financial management, fraud prevention and disciplinary procedures. the commission stated that it shared the parliament's view and that it believed that confidence in the objectivity of disciplinary proceedings would be strengthened if an external service was involved. it stated this in its white paper published on 1 march and will make detailed proposals for the reform of disciplinary law in the document on the whole of future disciplinary proceedings which it will publish in october. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to take them up in the course of the next partsession. many debates, and the report under consideration, have rightly pointed out that effective action to combat fraud at the expense of the european community's financial interests requires good cooperation and collaboration between the member states. article 280 of the treaty of amsterdam confirms this very clearly. it has also been rightly deplored that the convention adopted by the member states has been ratified by only a few of them. i thank all the speakers who also called on their countries of origin to take the necessary measures. olaf, the european anti-fraud office, is working hard to conclude cooperation agreements with the member states and, in specific areas, with other states. since the presentation of this report by uclaf, olaf, the european anti-fraud office, has been able to conclude an agreement with anti-mafia organisations in italy to ensure good cooperation at all levels and with all organisations involved in the fight against fraud. at the end of the week, a conference on this theme will be held in ancona. the commission welcomes the fact that some candidate countries have already taken steps to create and implement structures similar to those of the european anti-fraud office. poland, for example, has decided to set up and implement a polish olaf. i would also like to mention briefly the potential for legislative progress and to point out that the commission has proposed to the intergovernmental conference, which is responsible for amending the european treaties, to supplement the current system of protection of financial interests with a legal basis which would allow the creation of the european public prosecutor's office and the adoption of provisions on the criminal prosecution of crossborder fraud cases. the member states have indicated that they do not intend to amend the treaty in this area. the commission has not yet given up on this aspect, however, and will continue to clarify it and try to incorporate it into the intergovernmental conference. i would like to mention briefly the complaints which the commission has lodged against the european central bank and the european investment bank. in this case, the aim is to impose what parliament has precisely introduced in the regulation establishing olaf, namely that olaf is responsible for the fight against fraud in all the institutions of the european community. in the last few weeks, neither bank has made any moves. perhaps the case which was pending in the court of justice following the complaint lodged by certain members against the amendment of the rules of procedure of the european parliament was also put on hold. i simply think that with the provisional judgment of the court of first instance it has become clear that it is not a question of olaf's legal basis - and therefore the two banks can no longer isolate themselves or hide behind it - but simply, of course, of preserving the independence of the institutions. this has never been disputed, and neither has the european central bank. it is also a matter of asserting the immunity of members of parliament, which is a democratic achievement. it cannot be tampered with in any way. i would like to welcome the calls for the rule of law to be respected in all procedures, including olaf's work. i think the new director of olaf is also very strongly, very personally committed to this. we shall have the opportunity during the year to discuss other reports on the subject of the fight against fraud. the olaf monitoring committee, which ensures its independence, will shortly present its report. we'll have a chance to discuss it. i would point out that the commission is currently drawing up a basic strategy paper on the fight against fraud. this will certainly lead to further intensive and fruitful discussions. i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr bösch, for his report and i would also like, first of all, to thank this house for its long-term support for the establishment and work of olaf.

the rapporteur. - (de) mr president, the purpose of the directive is to detect and prevent subsidies which are liable to distort competition. to this end, the directive aims to require public and private undertakings with public service missions to keep separate accounts in such a way as to clearly distinguish between the reserved area and the area of free competition in the branch of activity. the directive is based on article 86 (3) and is therefore adopted exclusively by the commission. this is no longer in keeping with the spirit of the day and the way we conceive european legislation. it should therefore be amended. however, today's consultation is to be welcomed as an example of the new form of transparency in the commission's legislative work in areas where it also has control. it is also an example of the interest that commissioner monti and his services take in the opinion of the european parliament. the undertakings concerned have special or exclusive rights or provide services of general economic interest. it is therefore possible that cross-subsidisation may occur and cross-subsidisation complaints may be successful. thousands of companies will be affected. it is not clear that they actually consider the burden to be proportionate to the aims of the directive. the majority of the committee on economic and monetary affairs insisted on this regulation because more transparency is required within the internal market. in this respect, it is also the view of the whole committee, even if the rapporteur has defended a minority position in certain areas. it is not certain that the measure is genuinely appropriate to facilitate investigations in cases of suspected subsidisation causing distortions of competition, especially since there is no harmonised methodology at european level for internal accounting. i am expressing these reservations in order to give the commission the opportunity, in the course of its reworking, to dispel in a concrete and constructive way one or another of these doubts. i have already said that the commission expects complaints about cross-subsidies and has already in the past examined these complaints. however, the past has shown that the commission has always provided for sector-specific provisions, which exist in multiple regulatory areas. unfortunately, it did not continue in this direction. it can of course be said that it is easier to have a single regulation for the remaining sectors and this was also the view of the majority of the members of the economic and monetary affairs committee. i think, however, that every directive must also be checked in accordance with the principle of efficiency, precision and differentiation, so that the commission can perform its control function in an optimal way. there was still a problem with the consultations on this directive. the commission has not stressed that under article 295 of the ec treaty it is the exclusive competence of the member states to define services of general economic interest and the manner in which they are to be provided. by failing to make this point in the transparency directive, i wonder if the commission is not trying to take over some of this sovereignty and to empty the subsidiarity principle of its substance. it is for the member states to decide whether the offer of a broadcaster corresponds to the public service remit and whether all broadcasts should be included or not. the eu cannot intervene on this point. the text of the directive must therefore refer back to the amsterdam protocol, since it stipulates that it is also for the member states to determine the financial and organisational structures of public broadcasting systems and their specific activities. the aid to fulfil these public tasks is explicitly authorized and that is also what the majority of the economic and monetary affairs committee decided. however, in areas outside their public remit, broadcasting systems may the rapporteur. mr president, the subject at the end of this part-session is not fisheries but competition policy. we have discussed this subject in detail; the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. since i am regularly here on fridays, this does not seem very difficult to me. these are the exemption regulations which apply to the insurance sector in europe. you all know that competition law has been one of the main tasks of the european union, and therefore of the european commission, since the founding treaties. the competition rules are generally intended to ensure that competition is fair in the european internal market. this benefits consumers, promotes technical progress and prevents monopoly and cartels. there are strict rules for this purpose, and the commission must and can act accordingly. the three areas of application of these rules are: first, agreements or arrangements which are generally prohibited; second, abuse of a dominant position; and third, state aid. on all these points, the commission has always shown in the past that it takes the provisions of the treaty seriously. today we are discussing the first area. under certain conditions, the general prohibition on cartels is lifted: these are the exemption regulations. price fixing, limitation or control of production, the allocation of markets, the application of different conditions for equivalent services and additional contractual conditions, which are often very different in europe and exclude different services, are incompatible with the laws - even in areas governed by exemption regulations. under article 81 (3) exemption regulations may be allowed - please note this - provided that they help to reserve a fair share of the profit to the user and that no unnecessary restrictions are imposed which make competition impossible. in the insurance sector, we have had such a regulation since 1992 and until 2003. the commission is obliged to report on the operation of the regulation every six years and this report is submitted to us. this regulation on insurance block exemptions governs common rules, authorizes common rules for the agreement on the calculation of premiums, for the establishment of policy conditions, for the joint coverage of certain types of risks and for safety equipment. the agreements on the settlement of claims and on the registers for aggravated risks have not been taken up so far. as we adopted the rothley report on the harmonization of insurance against civil liability in respect of the use of motor vehicles at third reading on monday, i hope that the commission will be able to include the regulation on claims in this exemption regulation, because of this harmonized legal basis. the citizens of the european union will have a much easier life if they can in future settle claims with their own insurer for claims that have occurred abroad, even in a member state of the union, and if these agreements are also guaranteed by the commission in the framework of the exemption regulation. in its proposal parliament has, by a large majority, made a number of requests to the commission which it must take into account in its examination. this is the definition of market share in a world market, details questions about the first insurer for which this may not apply. if there is one large insurer and 20 smaller insurers, the large insurer cannot hold more than 10% of the market share in order for this exemption regulation to be accepted. we dare to doubt that it is fair. these issues are related to the possibility of termination. we want an insurance company to be able to withdraw after 6 months' notice and not just after 12 months. we want to provide a harmonised basis for european dispute settlement standards. on the whole, i can say that parliament is satisfied with this interim report and expects the commission to continue to develop and take stock of the insurance sector within the framework of the existing exemption regulations, all of which expire in 2002 and 2003, even for other sectors. i would like to ask for your agreement and thank you very much.

(de) mr president, unfortunately i have only a very short time to explain my opinion and that of the committee on legal affairs and the internal market on the question of the legal basis. in this case, it is not a matter of a discussion between lawyers with a dry heart, a kind of legal argument, but a highly political question, namely the question of jurisdiction and its delimitation. in such cases, a court does more than simply apply the law. he creates, shapes and develops law. as co-legislators, we would be well advised to take part in this process. and that's what we do by deciding for ourselves a demarcation, a demarcation of borders. let us briefly consider the following points: article 152 of the treaty excludes, expessis verbis, legal harmonisation in health matters. we may regret it - i understand that very well - but that is the way it is. article 95 - the general clause on the internal market - is the legal basis for the promotion of the internal market. and there is nothing wrong with this when health aspects are considered first. the question of delimitation and assessment is not a question of title. nor can it be based on the justification for such a directive, which the commission puts forward in a particularly repetitive and often quite incoherent form. nor can it be conducted as it was before, especially since the principle of subsidiarity has since been enshrined in the treaties. it can only be carried out with the objective content of a proposal and, in the case of amendments, with the objective content of those amendments. in this respect, the fact that there are special links with the internal market is not decisive. these still exist and could therefore, to be sure, render any delimitation absurd. it is never a question of whether the emphasis, the orientation of a directive is the promotion of the internal market, the elimination of trade barriers, the promotion of the free movement of goods, or whether it has some other emphasis. so far, no one has even claimed that this accent existed in this case. i therefore support the commission's proposal to reject the directive in its present form - i say 'in its present form' and not in any form whatsoever - on the grounds that it lacks a legal basis and infringes the principle of subsidiarity.

- (de) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to make seven points on this important subject. first, in 1991, the european heads of state and government expressly recognised the significant role of european political parties in article 138a of the treaty of amsterdam. they were guided by the idea that there could be no real democracy in the european union without european political parties having a secure legal basis and sound financial means. secondly, next year will mark 10 years since substantial progress was made on the legal status of european political parties and the treaty was brought to life. the group of the european people's party and the european democrats deeply deplores this. thirdly, we recall the important preparatory work in the framework of the tsatsos report, adopted in 1996, and also that of the kuhne report of 13 april 2000. other reports from the committee on budgets and the committee on budgetary control, and finally the report by our colleague mr ferber, have pointed out the urgency of a statute for political parties at european level and of corresponding regulations. fourthly, we are therefore pleased that the commission is prepared to support an addition to article 191 of the ec treaty on european political parties. we thank president prodi, commissioner barnier and the whole college for giving this request the importance it deserves. that will allow for a solution. we hope that the formulation chosen by the commission will allow for the rapid adoption of a statute for political parties at european level, that it will not set too high the necessary majority in the council and that it will respect the european parliament's full right of codecision. fifthly, we are also pleased that the european commission is obviously also confirming the possibility of action - if i am correctly informed - on the basis of article 308. the possibilities of article 308 must be exploited in so far as there is no supplement to the treaty. however, we firmly believe that a supplement to the treaty is the best way to find a solution. sixthly, the chairmen of the four largest groups in the european parliament - namely the group of the european people's party and the european democrats, the group of the party of european socialists, the group of the european liberal, democratic and reformist party and the group of the greens/european free alliance - have already submitted a proposal a few months ago, in agreement with the chairmen of the party federations and the commission, on the key elements of a statute for political parties at european level. they have thus demonstrated that this question must be resolved within the framework of a broad political consensus, and that it can be resolved. we hope that other groups, which do not yet have their own european parties, can also be associated with this consensus. seventhly and finally, we are also aware that until a statute for european political parties comes into force, we need transitional regulations governing and limiting the support of european political parties by the groups in the european parliament. we are prepared to take a broad initiative here, one that goes beyond political divisions. we want to continue to encourage the emancipation of european political parties from the groups and at the same time open up prospects for the future. our greatest wish is that european political parties should become an important vehicle for european political work. we want to give them that opportunity and above all we want to make sure that all these questions of support for european political parties are based on a transparent situation, a clear legal basis which can also be presented as such to the public. and this will not only serve the credibility of the parties, but also that of the european union and the european parliament.

of a general council meeting for approval by wto members, provided that the necessary internal procedures have been followed. at community level, this issue will still need to be discussed by the economy and will give added importance to the new round of wto negotiations, which we hope will be resumed as soon as possible. everyone must strive to achieve this. we hope that the accession process commission - mr president, i would like to begin by warmly joining a number of remarks made by the honourable member for westendorp - which i am sure is a reasonable way of starting a speech in a debate in the european parliament. first of all, let me share with you the unconcealed enthusiasm with which he praised my colleague, commissioner lamy, for the way he conducted these negotiations. i myself have had experience of negotiating with china and i must say that i remain impressed with the result achieved by commissioner lamy. i would like to say, as he himself has said with his characteristic generosity, that we all have to pay tribute to his predecessor, sir leon brittan, who is the originator of these negotiations, even if they have had to go several laps further than he had planned at the time. secondly, i fully agree with what the honourable member has said about the importance of the outcome of these negotiations. this agreement is very positive for china and europe; it's good for the asian region and for the rest of the world, and as we've seen, it certainly had a positive effect on the vote in the us congress. this is a positive agreement on the whole. this will be a challenge for china and, in time, for the wto. it has always seemed to me inappropriate to call the world trade organisation an institution in which between a fifth and a quarter of humanity is not represented. china's accession to the wto is good news. i would like to return to two questions raised by the chairman of the committee on industry, foreign trade, research and energy. first, the question of parliament's assent. commissioner lamy already had the opportunity to explain at the march part-session that the commission considered china's accession to the wto to be a trade agreement of major importance and that it was therefore the very type of agreement which would have to be submitted to parliament for assent, should the commission's proposals for the igc be accepted. we must not forget that these are still only proposals. we cannot extrapolate the outcome of the igc, that is certain. we must therefore abide by the rules of the present treaty. as parliament knows, the agreement with china does not fall into any of the categories described in rule 300 (3) which would justify parliament's assent. in principle, however, the agreement will be submitted to the european parliament for consultation, which will then have full latitude to express its views. of course, it is the council which decides to submit it to the european parliament for consultation. the institutional and legal response goes no further. on a more pragmatic and political level, i can assure the house that the commission will work with the european parliament in a spirit which will allow it to make its voice heard. the house is aware that commissioner lamy has set an example by speaking on several occasions with certain members during the last stages of negotiations with china. i know that he gave a report to the members of parliament just after the agreement was initialled: he telephoned the member to inform him of the conclusion of the agreement. i can assure this house that he intends to continue this dialogue throughout the internal approval procedures of the european union. this confirms the old adage that greater transparency invariably means greater success. at this point, however, i would like to add that the agreement we reached on 19 may is only a bilateral agreement on the terms of china's accession to the wto. the presidency stressed this in its speech. the multilateral phase of china's accession in geneva has yet to be finalised. the issue is not expected before the end of september at the earliest. in other words, whatever procedures are applied within the european union with regard to china's accession to the wto, it is only after the completion of the multilateral phase that the question will be considered. it is only after that date that the authorisation procedures will begin. i now come to a very important issue that the honourable member has raised about the technical assistance to be deployed to help china meet its wto obligations. the commission is implementing five cooperation programmes in china, totalling €25 million. some have already been started, others will be in the near future. in particular, there is a framework programme to strengthen relevant administrative structures and capacity, including through a series of specialised modules targeting specific segments of the chinese administration that will be responsible for the enforcement of wto rules. other programmes are designed to help china implement the specific obligations of wto membership. we are currently considering how best to consolidate them and we plan to launch new initiatives. china's accession to the wto and the considerable technical assistance needs that this entails are likely to generate great interest from other donors, including the us and japan, but also from our own member states and the wto secretariat. it is clear that close cooperation will be required to avoid overlaps and to develop synergies between the different programmes that each donor will implement in its own procedures. the need for coordination will be crucial when aid is concerned with the implementation of specific wto agreements. we will support the involvement of the wto in these areas. as regards the question of coordination with the united states, we will examine our options very carefully. we must not lose sight of the fact that this will have some repercussions on the visibility of our european efforts. the first exploratory talks to identify china's technical assistance needs and the respective roles and intentions of various donors will begin shortly. they will consist of direct exchanges with beijing and will take place on the sidelines of the wto working party on china's accession which meets next week. i just want to reiterate that this is an extremely important issue, which commissioner lamy and i have already started to discuss. we are determined to keep the european parliament fully informed of our plans. but i am certain that, in the face of this extremely important breakthrough, it is now crucial to give as comprehensive technical assistance as possible to china so that we can see the effects that we all hope to see in china, and therefore, in the rest of the region and the world.

the rapporteur. - (de) mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the treaty of amsterdam has finally opened the way to joint action in the field of asylum law and immigration and refugee policy. in my opinion, this was long overdue, because the decision to move from a simple economic community to political union itself was taken many years ago. it was therefore all the more important that the treaty of amsterdam had opened this way. unfortunately, on this occasion parliament was only granted the right to be heard in the development of the relevant legislation. i therefore expect the commission to continue despite the right of parliament to be associated in this area. regardless of this, one thing must be clear to parliament: from the moment we officially have only the right to be heard, we will only be able to influence the commission and the development of the legislation concerned effectively if we manage to agree on common principles and give up on achieving all our different political objectives. i think we have taken a good approach in the last few months when we discussed the commission's working document on this subject. i know that in my own group - i must add - no one fully agrees with this report. this is always the case when we seek consensus and find a compromise. we are largely satisfied, but rarely 100% satisfied. perhaps i should like to raise the points which i consider important for the future of the asylum procedure. first, we must find the strength to separate the three main groups, namely asylum, temporary reception of refugees from crisis regions and immigration policy. secondly, we must make sure that the admission procedure is shortened and simplified. at the same time, we must ensure the care and quality of the admission procedure. thirdly, the aim is that the asylum seeker has the right to lodge his application in only one eu member state. this means that we must ensure not only european harmonisation of procedural legislation but also harmonisation of the application of that legislation. this means that the staff dealing with asylum applications must be well trained. it must be possible for information to be available across borders. we must also ensure that asylum seekers enjoy the same framework conditions, regardless of the country in which they apply. this includes accommodation and board, in particular. the procedures must be identical whether the application is made in spain, germany or england. if we guarantee all this, it becomes logical to decree that only one application can be made. fourthly, i believe that eu member states should commit themselves to drawing up a single, binding list of visa-required countries on the one hand and third countries and safe countries of origin on the other. i know some people are critical of this. however, in my view, this is the only way to allow officials to decide on the same criteria and to create legal certainty in the member states for asylum seekers. another important point: we have stressed several times in the report that the burden must be shared between the member states. the details of this distribution are still to be discussed, but one thing is clear: it is no longer a matter of chance which door the majority of asylum seekers or refugees will knock on. the state chosen no longer has to bear the burden alone. i know that the right to asylum is a very difficult and politically sensitive subject. i think we have started a quality approach in the last few months in the committee discussion. we had a very
