i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. i am delighted to be able to speak to you on the last friday of this year - and i hope not the last one in strasbourg - here. as a member of the friday club, which is not registered but actually exists, i am one of the many members who are present on this day, as are you, and i hope that we can do the same next year. we will have to find ways of doing this. the report on a europe that includes all age groups, including the elderly, was very interesting to me as a non-senior: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work is a very good one. mrs flemming rightly pointed out that it is a good thing that people can age and still be healthy. the negative is that many of them are rejected, and the negative is that many of them have to feel excluded. the fact that people are discriminated against on grounds of age has been confirmed by my report on article 13, which i was able to present to the house in october. older workers are prevented from continuing training and from acquiring new technologies, even though they could. they are even denied the ability to learn and, even more so, the ability to innovate. they are being bullied into giving in and supposedly voluntarily quitting their jobs. discrimination is met with retaliation. they must be developed through model projects, and this in turn must be promoted through community initiatives such as equal. mrs sbarbati rightly calls for the commission's support for the proposal to restrict compulsory early retirement. i shall supplement it with experience from germany. early retirement schemes, which were initially well-intentioned by politicians, have been radically abused by some companies. they got paid - so the whole society was involved - older workers were being laid off, but younger workers were not being hired, and many positions were being eliminated. if we talk about finances, if you leave the workforce, you are entitled to a pension and not to be discriminated against by saying, "you get a handout for this". the european commission has recently published a report on the implementation of the european social fund. i hope that information campaigns in the member states will encourage older people to take part in social, cultural and social activities, in neighbourhood centres, in child and elder care centres, in associations and associations. we need these people, not just the so-called young dynamics and the successful ones! an effective strategy also includes promoting dialogue between generations. i am thinking of meeting in seminars, evaluating best practices, where older people pass on their knowledge and experience to younger people in the company. some people are younger at 70 than others at 17, just swimming with the current, not wanting to be noticed or noticed. if you settle for the average, you will never enter the adventure of a committed life. the many active older people should motivate us all to fight for a society in which solidarity between generations is not a phrase! (applause from the centre)
mr president, i have a little more time today than my group usually gives me. first of all, i would like to congratulate mr dary on his excellent report. i do not want to go into details because it is so good. the colleagues have already spoken about it. i just want to state a few simple truths at the end of the year. the first is that, as you said, public relations measures for the european agricultural model should be carried out here. i would like to make it clear that this european agricultural model implies that we still do not have the right to vote; i am not going to go into the details of the report, nor of the banana. we make our report, we do our work, and if the council doesn't like it, then they do what they want. nice has not made this progress either. i was a little sarcastic when i said yesterday that we had gone a step further; the opposite is of course true. i think that our efforts to get into the decision-making process must not be allowed to slacken. a few other truths: if we are talking about public relations but have to deal with bse, then perhaps it would be reasonable to understand that cows belong in the pasture. it's that simple. if they had stayed on the pastures, we wouldn't have bse. (applause from the centre) or when people talk about how we have a deficit in the protein supply. if the parliament's proposals, which have been adopted three times by a majority here - but this again shows parliament's impotence - were implemented, that the set-aside areas could be planted with legumes, with grass and that feeding would be allowed, then we would have had more basic feedingstuffs, more protein feedingstuffs. because then the cows would have stayed in the pasture and we wouldn't have had to feed the animal meal. the simple truth, when it is said that we cannot ensure the feeding of calves because there is no milk exchanger, the simple truth is that calves drink milk. if we want something for the vending machines, we can powder whole milk. the fact that we are mixing in the calves a fat that comes from animal meal production, which is already very worrying in terms of the transmission of bse, i think is a source of infection for young animals. why don't we say, "well, we'll put butter in the veal feed"? we've had enough of the products. here again the question of the european agricultural model arises. the next point concerns the promotion. there are firms of equal size, not small and large, but of equal size, where one gets 15,000 dm per worker and the other gets 150,000 dm per worker. that means he gets more than the labor costs. if i could get that much per worker in my 50-acre plant, i'd hire five more people. the five people i employ must be paid from production, not from what comes from brussels. we must also come to social criteria which ensure a certain degree of equality if we are to assume that agriculture is also intended to provide employment. mr verheugen, you know the debate about the new member states and the question of whether or not they get the compensation. if they get the compensation in the same way as here, we have the same problem, which is that we are not promoting work, but are basically setting in motion a machine for the destruction of work so that the bonuses that you get from brussels can be used in a lucrative way. the next point is when we talk about exports and intervention. we still have livestock transport, which is achieved by subsidizing the export of live animals. if we were to abolish this, we would no longer have to talk about the transport of animals and the images we have seen in the media. these are all things that we represent ourselves in the world through, and they're not positive, they're negative. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. she doesn't stand a chance. the only bright spot is the regulation on organic farming, and in germany there has been a lot of talk lately about the idea of a 'lead culture'. if we take organic farming as the guiding culture of agricultural policy, then i think we would have to come to other measures which are basically quite simple. we would then also have the opportunity to use public relations to inform the public, including the public outside europe, about our good food production and to convince them of this. (applause from the centre)
mr president, in my speech just now i did not have time to wish my colleagues a merry christmas and a happy new year. i'd like to make up for that. the second thing i wanted to say is that, despite all the criticisms, which i made clear in my speech, we are glad that this report has been adopted and that the commission is taking the initiative. it is true that there is a need and a justification for promoting the european agricultural model. all those who say that you can still have a taste of it in europe are right. you should do that on holidays too. but that does not change what i have made clear here earlier, namely that we must be careful even in the small things, that we must not forget the guiding culture of a social-ecological orientation in european agricultural policy and that we must always check whether the effects of the measures are in the right direction. i would like to make one more point. to return to the closure of the area, we could observe in practice that it is not the crop rotation that causes the closure of the area, but that the farms take up poor fields to carry out permanent closures here and carry out further intensification and chemization of the crop rotations in the other crop rotations. this completely defeats the purpose of this setaside, which was originally intended to bring about the greening of the crops in 1992. this is a good example of how small changes in practice can have a big impact. that was my petition this morning. that's what i was trying to point out. i hope that now that we are all convinced that we must bring about a change in agricultural policy, that we will now sit down together and do our homework to bring about the urgently needed correction in these small matters. happy holidays to you!
